newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's government not concerned by peseta level.
newsitem.headline: Spain's government not concerned by peseta level.

text.p: Spain's government is not worried by the current level of the peseta, Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez-Cascos said on Wednesday.

"The stability of the currency has aroused worries over exports, but it is always better that the peseta is a little more solid than expected," Cascos said in a speech on Spain's political and economic progress after 10 months in government.
The peseta has remained lodged in a band against the mark between 84.00 and 85.00 per mark in recent months and the Bank of Spain has intervened regularly to maintain this band.
In mid January Joaquim Molins, spokesman for Catalonia's CiU coalition which gives key backing to the ruling party, said he was concerned about the economic impact of the peseta's strength.
Cascos gave a favourable resume of Spain's economy over the past 10 months and said the consumer price index (CPI) and interest rates were advancing along a positive course.
